=== Budget English Auctions ===

Each player starts with 40 coins and a score of 0. Coins and scores are public. Each player has a private deck of 8 value cards: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, drawn in a secret random order. Seats are numbered 1 to n.

The game lasts 8 rounds. Each round:
1. Deal: every player privately sees the next card of their own deck. That is their value for this round's item. Every card is used exactly once over the game.
2. Talk: every player writes one short message at the same time without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Messages are not binding and change nothing.
3. Bidding: the standing bid is 0 and there is no leader. Every player starts active. There are up to 3 bidding steps. In each step, every active player who is not the current leader chooses at the same time either to RAISE or to DROP. A RAISE names a whole number at least the standing bid + 2, and no more than that player's current coins. A player who DROPs is out of this round's auction and is not asked again this round. A player with fewer coins than the standing bid + 2 must drop and is not asked. The leader is not asked and stays in.
4. Resolve each step: if at least one player raised, the highest raise becomes the standing bid and its bidder becomes the leader. Ties for the highest raise go to the tied player with the lowest score; if still tied, to the tied player whose seat comes first counting from seat ((r-1) mod n)+1 upward and wrapping around. Players who raised but were outbid remain active. The standing bid, the leader and who dropped are announced. If nobody raised in a step, bidding ends immediately. Bidding also ends after step 3.
5. Settle: if there is a leader, the leader pays the standing bid from their coins and their score changes by (their value - standing bid), which may be negative. The leader's value is announced; nobody else's value is revealed. If nobody ever raised, the item goes unsold and nothing changes.
6. Unspent coins carry over to the next round.

After round 8 the game ends. The highest score wins. If scores are tied for the top, the tied player with more coins remaining wins. If still tied, the game is a draw shared among them.

The game lasts 8 rounds. Each round:
1. Deal: every player privately sees the next card of their own deck. That is their value for this round's item. Every card is used exactly once over the game.
2. Talk: every player writes one short message at the same time without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Messages are not binding and change nothing.
3. Bidding: the standing bid is 0 and there is no leader. Every player starts active. There are up to 3 bidding steps. In each step, every active player who is not the current leader chooses at the same time either to RAISE or to DROP. A RAISE names a whole number at least the standing bid + 2, and no more than that player's current coins. A player who DROPs is out of this round's auction and is not asked again this round. A player with fewer coins than the standing bid + 2 must drop and is not asked. The leader is not asked and stays in.
4. Resolve each step: if at least one player raised, the highest raise becomes the standing bid and its bidder becomes the leader. Ties for the highest raise go to the tied player with the lowest score; if still tied, to the tied player whose seat comes first counting from seat ((r-1) mod n)+1 upward and wrapping around. Players who raised but were outbid remain active. The standing bid, the leader and who dropped are announced. If nobody raised in a step, bidding ends immediately. Bidding also ends after step 3.
5. Settle: if there is a leader, the leader pays the standing bid from their coins and their score changes by (their value - standing bid), which may be negative. The leader's value is announced; nobody else's value is revealed. If nobody ever raised, the item goes unsold and nothing changes.
6. Unspent coins carry over to the next round.

Each player starts with 40 coins and a score of 0. Coins and scores are public. Each player has a private deck of 8 value cards: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, drawn in a secret random order. Seats are numbered 1 to n.

The game lasts 8 rounds. Each round:
1. Deal: every player privately sees the next card of their own deck. That is their value for this round's item. Every card is used exactly once over the game.
2. Talk: every player writes one short message at the same time without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Messages are not binding and change nothing.
3. Bidding: the standing bid is 0 and there is no leader. Every player starts active. There are up to 3 bidding steps. In each step, every active player who is not the current leader chooses at the same time either to RAISE or to DROP. A RAISE names a whole number at least the standing bid + 2, and no more than that player's current coins. A player who DROPs is out of this round's auction and is not asked again this round. A player with fewer coins than the standing bid + 2 must drop and is not asked. The leader is not asked and stays in.
4. Resolve each step: if at least one player raised, the highest raise becomes the standing bid and its bidder becomes the leader. Ties for the highest raise go to the tied player with the lowest score; if still tied, to the tied player whose seat comes first counting from seat ((r-1) mod n)+1 upward and wrapping around. Players who raised but were outbid remain active. The standing bid, the leader and who dropped are announced. If nobody raised in a step, bidding ends immediately. Bidding also ends after step 3.
5. Settle: if there is a leader, the leader pays the standing bid from their coins and their score changes by (their value - standing bid), which may be negative. The leader's value is announced; nobody else's value is revealed. If nobody ever raised, the item goes unsold and nothing changes.
6. Unspent coins carry over to the next round.

1. Deal: every player privately sees the next card of their own deck. That is their value for this round's item. Every card is used exactly once over the game.
2. Talk: every player writes one short message at the same time without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Messages are not binding and change nothing.
3. Bidding: the standing bid is 0 and there is no leader. Every player starts active. There are up to 3 bidding steps. A player with fewer coins than the standing bid + 2 must drop and is not asked. The leader is not asked and stays in.
4. Resolve each step: if at least one player raised, the highest raise becomes the standing bid and its bidder becomes the leader. The game lasts 8 rounds. Each round:
1. Deal: every player privately sees the next card of their own deck. That is their value for this round's item. Every card is used exactly once over the game.
2. Talk: every player writes one short message at the same time without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Messages are not binding and change nothing.
3. Bidding: the standing bid is 0 and there is no leader. Every player starts active. There are up to 3 bidding steps. In each step, every active player who is not the current leader chooses at the same time either to RAISE or to DROP. A RAISE names a whole number at least the standing bid + 2, and no more than that player's current coins. A player who DROPs is out of this round's auction and is not asked again this round. A player with fewer coins than the standing bid + 2 must drop and is not asked. The leader is not asked and stays in.
4. Resolve each step: if at least one player raised, the highest raise becomes the standing bid and its bidder becomes the leader. Ties for the highest raise go to the tied player with the lowest score; if still tied, to the tied player whose seat comes first counting from seat ((r-1) mod n)+1 upward and wrapping around. Players who raised but were outbid remain active. The standing bid, the leader and who dropped are announced. If nobody raised in a step, bidding ends immediately. Bidding also ends after step 3.

6. Unspent coins carry over to the next round.
